chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid and Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Yahya Al-Halabi, from Harun ibn Kharjah, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), regarding the Statement of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:
Surely Allah has raised Talut to be a king over you.
They said: How can he have kingship over us while we are more deserving of it than him? He (peace be upon him) said: He was neither from the lineage of the Prophets nor from the lineage of the kings.
He said: Surely Allah has chosen him in preference to you.

And He said: Surely the sign of his kingship is that there shall come to you the chest in which there is tranquillity from your Lord and residue of the relics of what the children of Musa and the children of Harun have left, the angels bearing it.
And Allah, Glorious is His mention, said: Surely Allah will try you with a river; whoever then drinks from it, he is not of me, and whoever does not taste of it, he is surely of me.
So they drank from it except for three hundred and thirteen men. From them were those who drank, and those who did not drink.
So when it was time for duel, the ones who had drunk said: We have today no power against Jalut and his forces.
And those who did not drink said: How often has a small party vanquished a numerous host by Allah's permission, and Allah is with the patient.

key_terms.التَّابُوتُ: The Ark or Chest containing relics
key_terms.طالُوتَ: Talut (Saul), the first king of Bani Israel

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the 313 men who did not drink from the river in the story of Talut?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elucidates the divine selection of Talut (Saul), emphasizing that his legitimacy stemmed not from prophetic or royal lineage but from Allah’s direct choice and the sign of the Tabut. The text highlights the trial of the river as a filter for spiritual discipline, where the faithful few who abstained from excessive drinking were distinguished by their patience (sabr) to defeat Jalut (Goliath), a theme often linked to the Battle of Badr in Shia exegesis.

en.sarwar: 499. From him, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al-Husayn Bin Saeed, from Fazaalat Bin Ayyub, from Yahya Al-Jalby, from Abdullah Bin Suleyman, who has narrated the following: Abu Ja’far (a.s.) said after reciting:

“Surely the sign of His kingdom is, that there shall come to you the chest in which there is tranquillity from your Lord and residue of the relics of what the children of Musa and the children of Haroun have left, the angels bearing it”[2:248].
He (a.s.) said: ‘They are described in the Verse of ‘Al-Baqra’.
